pH - Soils with extremely high or extremely low values of pH may not be conducive to plant growth. Soils with pH values less than 7.0 are acidic in reaction, while a pH higher than 7.0 indicates a basic or alkaline reaction. With few exceptions the overburden and interburden material analyzed was alkaline. Most samples fell within the range 7.5 to 8.5, although some samples were highly alkaline (pH greater than 8.9). One highly acid sample (pH=3.8) was identified from the Stray No. 1 coal seam on Tract III.
Soluble Salts - A saline soil is one in which the saturation extract has an electrical conductivity (EC) greater than 4.0 mmhos/cm. Plant species vary widely in their tolerance to soluble salts, with many species utilized in revegetation considered to be salt tolerant. A number of saline intervals were identified, but in most cases the degree of salinity was low (EC less than 6.0). Of approximately 750 samples a total of 23 were highly saline (EC greater than 8.0). Most saline intervals were in the upper 20 feet of overburden, although some interburden intervals were saline also. Data from six holes indicate that complete mixing would not reduce EC values to less than 4.0. Weighted average values of EC in these cases range from 4.0 to 6.6.
Exchangeable Sodium - High levels of exchangeable sodium in combination with expanding lattice clays can result in poor tilth and impaired water penetration, root penetration and aeration.
